body.sourceEnglish:
Soil contains many kinds of living organisms. Bacteria and fungi help break down organic matter and cycle nutrients.

Some fungi help roots take up nutrients. Worm channels can help water and air enter soil.

Look at roots, soil structure and water movement as well as visible soil life.

Put soil and water in a clear jar, with a little suitable dispersing detergent. Close and shake it, then leave it undisturbed.

Sand settles first. Silt settles next, while clay can remain suspended much longer.

This is a rough learning exercise. Clumps and unsettled clay can mislead you; use a soil laboratory when accurate texture is needed.

A thick sand layer beneath cloudy water does not yet tell you the final proportions. Some fine particles may still be suspended.

Compare the settled layers and feel the soil in the field.

Record what you see and what remains uncertain. Do not prescribe watering or soil treatments from one jar alone.

Compaction, poor drainage and loss of organic matter can limit roots and soil life.

Pale colour or few worms do not prove that chemicals killed the soil. Worm activity also changes with moisture and season.

Look for patterns across the field. Check management history, drainage and plant growth before choosing a remedy.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Mavu a na mifuda minzhi ya zwithu zwine zwa tshila. Bacteria na fungi dzi thusa u break down organic matter na u cycle nutrients.

Dziṅwe fungi dzi thusa midzi u dzhia nutrients. Worm channels dzi nga thusa uri maḓi na muya zwi dzhene mavuni.

Sedzani midzi, tshivhumbeo tsha mavu na u tshimbila ha maḓi, ni dovhe ni sedze zwithu zwi tshilaho zwine zwa vhonala mavuni.

Vheani mavu na maḓi kha jar ine na kona u vhona zwa nga ngomu hayo, ni engedze suitable dispersing detergent ṱhukhu. Ni vale jar, ni i dzinginye, ni i sie i sa tshintshwi.

Sand i dzula fhasi u thoma. Silt i dzula fhasi nga murahu, ngeno clay i tshi nga sala i suspended lwa tshifhinga tshilapfu vhukuma.

Hezwi ndi nyito ya u guda ya u anganyela. Clumps na clay i sa athu u dzula fhasi zwi nga ni xedza; shumisani soil laboratory musi accurate texture i tshi ṱoḓea.

Thick sand layer nga fhasi ha cloudy water a i athu u ni vhudza final proportions. Fine particles dzi nga kha ḓi vha suspended.

Vhambedzani layers dze dza dzula fhasi, ni dovhe ni fare mavu tsimuni.

Ṅwalani zwe na zwi vhona na zwine zwa kha ḓi sa vha khagala. Ni songo dzhia phetho ya u sheledza kana u lafha mavu nga u sedza jar nthihi fhedzi.

Compaction, poor drainage na u xela ha organic matter zwi nga limit midzi na vhutshilo ha mavu.

Pale colour kana worms dzi si gathi a zwi khwaṱhisedzi uri chemicals dzo vhulaha mavu. U shuma ha worms na hone hu a shanduka u ya nga vhunyunyu na khalaṅwaha.

Sedzani patterns tsimuni yoṱhe. Sedzani ḓivhazwakale ya nḓila ya u langa tsimu, drainage na u aluwa ha zwimela ni sa athu khetha nḓila ya u tandulula thaidzo.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Use several clues to assess soil condition
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Shumisani zwiṱalusi zwo vhalaho u ṱola vhuimo ha mavu.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Soil colour and worm counts alone do not diagnose the cause of a problem
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Muvhala wa mavu na tshivhalo tsha zwivhungu fhedzi a zwi sumbedzi uri thaidzo yo vhangwa nga mini.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A jar exercise gives a rough indication of texture, not a complete soil test
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: U lingedza nga jar zwi sumbedza texture nga u anganyela fhedzi, a si soil test yo fhelelaho.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Check drainage, roots and management history before choosing a remedy
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Ṱolani drainage, midzi na ḓivhazwakale ya nḓila ya u langa tsimu ni sa athu khetha nḓila ya u tandulula thaidzo.

question.sourceEnglish: A soil jar still has cloudy water above the sand layer. What should the farmer conclude?
question.tshivendaDraft: Jar ya mavu i kha ḓi vha na cloudy water nga nṱha ha lera la sand. Mulimi u fanela u phetha mini?

options.sourceEnglish: The soil definitely needs less water
options.tshivendaDraft: Mavu a ṱoḓa maḓi o fhungudzeaho nga ngoho

options.sourceEnglish: Fine particles may still be suspended; more observation is needed
options.tshivendaDraft: Fine particles dzi nga kha ḓi vha suspended; u sedza hafhu zwi a ṱoḓea

options.sourceEnglish: All the clay has already settled
options.tshivendaDraft: Clay yoṱhe yo no dzula fhasi

options.sourceEnglish: The crop definitely needs gypsum
options.tshivendaDraft: Tshimela tshi ṱoḓa gypsum nga ngoho

rationale.sourceEnglish: Cloudy water can contain unsettled fine particles. One early observation cannot establish the final proportions or the right treatment.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Cloudy water i nga vha na fine particles dzi sa athu u dzula fhasi. U sedza ha u thoma luthihi a hu nga khwaṱhisedzi final proportions kana treatment yo teaho.

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer finds compacted soil and few worms. What is the useful next step?
question.tshivendaDraft: Mulimi u wana mavu o compacted na worms dzi si gathi. Ndi vhukando vhufhio vhu tevhelaho vhune ha nga thusa?

options.sourceEnglish: Assume every soil organism has died
options.tshivendaDraft: Humbulani uri soil organism iṅwe na iṅwe yo fa

options.sourceEnglish: Add a treatment without checking the site
options.tshivendaDraft: Engedzani treatment ni songo ṱola fhethu.

options.sourceEnglish: Check drainage, roots, moisture and management history
options.tshivendaDraft: Ṱolani drainage, midzi, vhunyunyu na ḓivhazwakale ya nḓila ya u langa tsimu.

options.sourceEnglish: Give up because the soil cannot improve
options.tshivendaDraft: Litshani u lingedza ngauri mavu a nga si khwinifhadzee

rationale.sourceEnglish: Several observations help identify a problem. Worm activity varies with conditions, so few worms alone do not establish its cause.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: U sedza zwithu zwo vhalaho zwi thusa u wana thaidzo. Worm activity i a shanduka u ya nga zwiimo, ngauralo worms dzi si gathi fhedzi a dzi khwaṱhisedzi uri thaidzo yo vhangwa nga mini.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: A compost heap cut open, showing alternating layers of dry brown material and fresh green material, heat rising from the middle, and an arrow showing it being turned.
infographicAlt.tshivendaDraft: Heap ya compost cut open i sumbedza alternating layers dza dry brown material na fresh green material. Heat i gonya i tshi bva vhukati; arrow i sumbedza uri heap i a rembuluswa.

title.tshivendaDraft: U Ita na U Shumisa Khomposo (Compost)

body.sourceEnglish:
Compost is organic matter broken down under managed conditions.

Finished compost can improve soil structure and contribute nutrients.

Time to readiness varies with materials, moisture, air and temperature. A province name or a fixed number of weeks is not a readiness test.

Mix dry browns with fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.

If the heap becomes slimy or smells strongly of ammonia, add dry browns and turn it.

Check moisture and air as the heap changes; one recipe does not suit every mix of materials.

A hot centre does not prove that every part of a heap has been treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.

Keep meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste and contaminated materials out of this simple household system.

Do not assume home composting destroys every weed seed or disease organism. Use a recognised process where sanitation is required.

Keep wattle seed pods out of the compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.

Use only clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; its name alone is not proof that it is free of contamination.

Check the heap and turn when it needs more air or mixing. Keep it moist rather than waterlogged.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Compost ndi organic matter yo broken down nga fhasi ha zwiimo zwi langulwaho.

Compost yo fhelelaho i nga khwinifhadza tshivhumbeo tsha mavu, na u engedza nutrients.

Tshifhinga tsha u luga ha manyoro tshi a fhambana u ya nga zwishumiswa (materials), vhunyunyu, muya na thempheretsha (temperature). Dzina ḽa vundu kana mbalo yo vhewaho ya vhege a si tsedzuluso ya u luga ha manyoro.

Tanganyani dry browns na fresh greens. Iledzani thick, wet layers dzi thivhelaho muya u dzhena.

Arali thulwi ya manyoro ya vha slimy kana ya nukha ammonia nga maanḓa, shelani dry browns nahone ni i rembuluse.

Sedzulusani vhunyunyu na muya musi thulwi i tshi khou shanduka; nḓila nthihi ya u ṱanganya a i lulameli muṱanganyo muṅwe na muṅwe wa zwishumiswa.

Vhukati ho fhisaho a vhu khwaṱhisedzi uri tshipida tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe tsha thulwi tsho treated. Tshifhinga, temperature na ndangulo zwoṱhe zwi na ndeme.

Iledzani u dzhenisa nyama, dairy, zwimela zwi re na malwadze, pet waste na contaminated materials kha iyi nḓila i leluwaho ya muṱani.

Ni songo humbula uri home composting i fhedza weed seed iṅwe na iṅwe kana disease organism iṅwe na iṅwe. Shumisani recognised process hune sanitation ya ṱoḓea.

Iledzani u dzhenisa wattle seed pods kha thulwi ya manyoro. Thulwi yo ḓoweleaho i nga kha ḓi sa ita uri mbeu iṅwe na iṅwe i vhe non-viable.

Shumisani zwishumiswa zwo kunaho, zwi songo treated fhedzi. Bark i a sina nga u ongowa; dzina layo fhedzi a si vhuṱanzi ha uri a i na contamination.

Sedzulusani thulwi ni i rembuluse musi i tshi toda muya wo engedzeaho kana u tanganiswa. I vhulungeni i na vhunyunyu, hu si waterlogged.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Balance browns, greens, moisture and air
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Linganyisani browns, greens, vhunyunyu na muya.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A hot centre does not prove the whole heap is sanitised
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Vhukati ho fhisaho a vhu sumbedzi uri thulwi yoṱhe yo sanitised.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep seed pods and contaminated materials out
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Siyani seed pods na contaminated materials nnḓa ha thulwi.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Judge readiness from the compost condition, not a fixed regional timetable
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Ṱolani uri compost yo lugela nga tshiimo tshayo; ni songo shumisa timetable ya dzingu yo vhewaho.

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer's compost heap smells strongly of ammonia and is wet and slimy. What's the fix?
question.tshivendaDraft: Thulwi ya compost ya mulimi i nukha ammonia nga maanḓa nahone i na maḓi na slimy. Ndi mini zwine zwa nga lugisa?

options.sourceEnglish: Add more nitrogen-rich green material
options.tshivendaDraft: Engedzani green material ine ya vha na nitrogen nnzhi

options.sourceEnglish: Add more dry carbon material like straw and turn the heap
options.tshivendaDraft: Engedzani zwinzhi zwa material ya carbon yo omaho, sa straw, nahone ni rembuluse thulwi ya compost.

options.sourceEnglish: Stop turning it and let it cool
options.tshivendaDraft: Litshani u rembulusa thulwi, ni i tende i rothole.

options.sourceEnglish: Add more water — the smell means it's too dry
options.tshivendaDraft: Engedzani maḓi manzhi — honoyo munukho u amba uri yo oma nga maanḓa

rationale.sourceEnglish: A wet, slimy heap may need more air and drier material. Add dry browns and turn the heap to open it up. An ammonia smell can also suggest too much nitrogen-rich material. Check that the heap stays damp, not soggy.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Thulwi i re na maḓi na slimy i nga ṱoḓa muya wo engedzeaho na zwishumiswa zwo omaho u fhira zwa zwino. Engedzani dry browns ni rembuluse thulwi uri i vulee. Munukho wa ammonia u nga dovha wa sumbedza uri hu na nitrogen-rich material nnzhi nga maanḓa. Sedzani uri thulwi i dzule i na vhunyunyu, hu si soggy.

question.sourceEnglish: Why keep wattle seed pods out of an ordinary compost heap?
question.tshivendaDraft: Ndi ngani ni tshi tea u vhea wattle seed pods nnḓa ha thulwi ya compost yo ḓoweleaho?

options.sourceEnglish: Bark makes every heap too hot
options.tshivendaDraft: Bark i ita uri thulwi iṅwe na iṅwe i fhise nga maanḓa

options.sourceEnglish: Some seeds may survive and spread when the compost is used
options.tshivendaDraft: Dziṅwe seeds dzi nga tshila nahone dza phaḓalala musi compost i tshi shumiswa

options.sourceEnglish: Pods always attract termites
options.tshivendaDraft: Pods dzi kunga termites tshifhinga tshoṱhe

options.sourceEnglish: Pods release a gas that kills every soil organism
options.tshivendaDraft: Pods dzi bvisa gas ine ya vhulaha zwivhumbiwa zwoṱhe zwa mavu

rationale.sourceEnglish: An ordinary heap may not expose every seed to conditions that make it non-viable. Excluding pods avoids spreading them with the compost.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Thulwi yo ḓoweleaho i nga kha ḓi sa swikisa mbeu iṅwe na iṅwe kha zwiimo zwine zwa ita uri i vhe non-viable. U bvisa pods zwi thivhela uri dzi phaḓalale dzi tshi ṱuwa na compost.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Two patches of soil under the same sun: bare ground cracked and dry, mulched ground still dark and moist.
infographicAlt.tshivendaDraft: Zwipiḓa zwivhili zwa mavu nga fhasi ha ḓuvha ḽithihi: mavu a songo fukedzwaho o pwashekanaho nahone o oma; mavu o funedzwaho nga mulch a kha ḓi vha na muvhala wa swiswi nahone a tshe na vhunyunyu.

title.sourceEnglish: Mulching and Cover Crops: Protecting and Building Soil
title.tshivendaDraft: Mulching and Cover Crops: U tsireledza mavu na Building Soil

body.sourceEnglish:
Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.

Mulch can reduce evaporation, soften the impact of rain and suppress weeds.

Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.

Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.

The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.

Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.

Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.

Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.

Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.

A Highveld field left bare after the maize harvest faces two main risks.

Winter wind can carry away dry topsoil.

The first heavy spring storm can strike bare ground and damage its surface and structure. If water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.

Cover crops, mulch, and organic matter can help hold soil in place and help it stay alive.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Fukedzani mavu a songo fukwaho nga mulch yo kunaho, yo teaho, u fana na straw, hatsi ho omaho kana wood chips.

Mulch i nga fhungudza evaporation; i nga fhungudza u rwa ha mvula; i nga thivhela weeds.

I vhetseni kule na trunks and stems. Sedzani vhunyunyu nga fhasi hayo ni lulamise layer; mulch nnzhi a i dzuli i tshi vha yavhuḓi.

Cover crops dzi nga tsireledza mavu vhukati ha main crops. Khethani u ya nga mutsho wa henefho, maḓi ane a vha hone na u zwala hu tevhelaho.

Tsumbo dza ngudo dzi katela oats, lupins, sunn hemp na cowpea. Sedzani arali dzi tshi fanela fhethu haṋu ni sa athu dzi zwala.

Legumes dzi ṱoḓa bacteria dzo teaho na zwiimo zwo teaho zwa u mela u fix nitrogen. Nutrients dzi re kha masalela adzo dzi a wanala musi material i tshi decompose.

Worm farms dzi nga shandula food scraps na bedding zwo teaho zwa vha castings. Sedzani tshifaredzi, ni songo lavhelela ḓuvha ḽo vhewaho ḽa u kaṋa.

Liquid i elelaho nga mvelo i tshi bva kha worm bin i vhidzwa leachate. A si tshithu tshithihi na worm-casting tea yo lugiswaho.

Leachate i nga vha na harmful organisms kana zwithu zwi re na khombo. Ni songo i shumisa kha edible plants kana u humbula uri dilution i ita uri i vhe yo tsireledzeaho.

Tsimu ya Highveld yo salaho i songo fukedzwa nga murahu ha u kaṋa maize i sedzana na khombo mbili khulwane.

Mhepo ya vhuria i nga hwala topsoil yo omaho ya i bvisa.

Storm ya u thoma khulwane ya spring i nga rwa mavu a songo fukedzwaho, ya tshinyadza surface na structure ya hone. Arali maḓi a tshi elela nṱha ha tsimu, a nga hwala loosened soil a a bvisa.

Cover crops, mulch na organic matter zwi nga thusa u fara mavu fhethu hayo na u thusa uri a dzule a tshi khou tshila.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Protect exposed soil with suitable cover
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Tsireledzani mavu a songo fukedzwaho nga zwithu zwo teaho zwa u fukedza.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep mulch away from trunks and stems
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Vhetseni mulch kule na trunks na stems.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Choose cover crops for local water, weather and the following crop
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Khethani cover crops u ya nga maḓi a henefho, mutsho na crop i tevhelaho.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Worm-bin leachate is not automatically safe fertiliser; keep it off edible plants
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Worm-bin leachate a i sokou vha fertiliser yo tsireledzeaho; i vhetseni kule na edible plants.

question.sourceEnglish: A Highveld farmer harvests maize in April and leaves the field bare all winter. What are the two main risks?
question.tshivendaDraft: Mulimi wa Highveld u kaṋa maize nga April a sia tsimu i songo fukedzwaho vhuria hoṱhe. Ndi khombo dzifhio mbili khulwane?

options.sourceEnglish: Overheating in winter sun and waterlogging from rain
options.tshivendaDraft: U fhisa nga maanḓa fhasi ha ḓuvha ḽa vhuria na waterlogging i bvaho kha mvula

options.sourceEnglish: Frost kills soil life and weeds take over early
options.tshivendaDraft: Frost i vhulaha zwivhumbiwa zwi tshilaho mavuni, weeds dzi dzhia fhethu nga u ṱavhanya

options.sourceEnglish: Wind erosion of dry topsoil and loss of soil structure from spring storm impact
options.tshivendaDraft: Wind erosion ya topsoil yo omaho na u tshinyala ha soil structure nga u rwa ha spring storm

options.sourceEnglish: Soil pH drops and nitrogen builds up
options.tshivendaDraft: Soil pH i tsela fhasi na nitrogen i a kuvhangana

rationale.sourceEnglish: Bare soil is exposed to winter wind, which can carry away dry topsoil. Raindrop impact can damage the surface; where water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Mavu a songo fukedzwaho a vha khagala kha mhepo ya vhuria, ine ya nga hwala topsoil yo omaho ya i bvisa. U rwa ha marothi a mvula hu nga tshinyadza surface; hune maḓi a elela nṱha ha tsimu, a nga hwala loosened soil a a bvisa.

question.sourceEnglish: What should you remember about liquid draining from a worm bin?
question.tshivendaDraft: Ni fanela u humbula mini nga liquid i elelaho i tshi bva kha worm bin?

options.sourceEnglish: It is always safe on salad leaves
options.tshivendaDraft: I dzula yo tsireledzea tshifhinga tshoṱhe kha maṱari a saladi.

options.sourceEnglish: It can contain harmful organisms or substances; dilution is not a safety guarantee
options.tshivendaDraft: I nga vha na harmful organisms kana zwithu zwi re na khombo; dilution a si safety guarantee

options.sourceEnglish: It is identical to finished worm castings
options.tshivendaDraft: I fana tshoṱhe na finished worm castings

options.sourceEnglish: A fixed dilution makes every liquid safe
options.tshivendaDraft: Dilution yo vhewaho i ita uri liquid iṅwe na iṅwe i vhe yo tsireledzeaho

rationale.sourceEnglish: Leachate is liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin. Its composition varies, so it must not be presented as a guaranteed safe feed for edible crops.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Leachate ndi liquid i elelaho nga mvelo i tshi bva kha worm bin. Composition yayo i a fhambana, ngauralo a i tei u sumbedzwa sa feed yo khwaṱhisedzwaho uri yo tsireledzea kha edible crops.

precisionConclusions: Retain exact physical settling/layers and pale colour in ambiguous candidates.
Retain source thick/wet rather than large/crowded/much water.
Reject root growth narrowing of broad root limits.
Keep rough exercise, unsettled clay, CAN mislead and WHEN laboratory accuracy needed exact.
Prior no-edible-use and no-dilution-safety assumptions outside scoped units remain unchanged.
Preserve exact reviewed harmful OR substances / safety guarantee option anchor.
No invented species, amounts, dates, durations, treatment or fertility promise.

primaryEvidence.scope: Supports dark label, no colour intensity/texture/soil diagnosis approval.
tsitsikana occurs for an area crowded with buildings; does not establish physical layer thickness.
Uses vhudenya for ice thickness; supports distinguishing thickness from generic largeness.
mutswi appears in theft passage, not independently established as arrow. English arrow retained; no guessed translation substituted.

lexicalLimits: Primary search-index excerpts only; no new fluent/local farming approval. No primary evidence established proposed pale, loosened, lera or measured-texture terms in the required physical meaning. These uncertain terms are held precisely rather than blanket-approved.
